notes.10: This trigonometry question was generally answered well. The most common errors were using sine rather than cosine, premature rounding, or truncating the answer. Some candidates who did know to use cosine wrote the fraction the wrong way round. Answer 10.7 11 Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0580 Mathematics June 2011
notes.11: Having met trigonometry in Question 10 some candidates continued using it for this question. However many used Pythagoras’ theorem and gave the correct answer. Some lost one mark for not giving the answer to at least 3 significant figures. Others hadn’t realised that the required length had to be less than 12 and gave the answer as 15 from adding 12 squared and 9 squared and square rooting. Answer 7.94
notes.12: (a) This part was well answered by candidates who were confident in using standard form. There were a significant number of candidates who were not familiar with standard form and some just rounded the answer. (b) Well answered by some candidates. Many were able to earn one mark for performing the calculation, but then not putting the answer into the required standard form. 7 -2 Answers (a) 1.646 × 10 (b) 3.32 × 10
notes.13: (a) Candidates were generally successful in this part. A wide variety of incorrect answers was seen from unsuccessful candidates. (b) Many candidates were able to score both marks. The common errors were converting the fractions to decimals, and not showing the improper fraction 7/6. Others did not show cancelling or a fraction equivalent to 12/21. The question clearly stated that candidates should write down all the steps in their working. Answers (a) 36
notes.14: (a) Candidates struggled with this part and many gave the answer 0.055, clearly confused by centilitres. (b) Candidates were more successful in this part. notes.15: (a) This part was the best answered of the three parts. Many candidates, however, appeared not to be familiar with the word ‘integer’ and many gave the answer to one decimal place. (b) Candidates appeared to be confused by significant figures in a decimal number. The most common incorrect answer was 0.003 i.e. 3 decimal places. (c) Few candidates were able to give the required bound and 53.3 was often seen. Answers (a) 67 (b) 0.00304 (c) 56.35

notes.17: (a) This was the least successful part in the whole paper. Very few candidates appeared to know the term ‘reflex’. Many gave ‘acute’ as the answer from the wrong part of the angle. The other common answer was exterior. (b) (i) Many candidates were able to draw a trapezium if they ordered the letters correctly. Several drew parallelograms. notes.18: Candidates are generally becoming more familiar with compound interest. However there is a tendency to use the formula. This is fine but often candidates do not understand how to apply it. Some candidates used simple interest instead. Answer 127.31
